body: Web crawling is a major source of large language model (LLM) pretraining data, yet data-selection pipelines discard a large share of crawled pages. We investigate how a crawler should allocate its budget across and within hosts to collect more high-quality pretraining data. Combining document-level quality classifier scores, web-graph centrality metrics, and Common Crawl's per-host crawl coverage, we find that roughly half of the variation in classifier scores occurs between hosts. In the crawls we analyze, a few pages from a host also provide a useful estimate of the quality of its remaining pages. Common Crawl uses harmonic centrality, a graph centrality metric, to guide its crawl allocation. In our simulations, using centrality to choose which hosts to crawl yields limited gains over random ordering and performs worse for some classifiers. For deciding how deeply to crawl each host, sampling a few pages and then fetching more from hosts with higher-scoring samples collects several times more high-quality pages per fetch than uniform depth or centrality-based allocation. Finally, Common Crawl's observed per-host coverage has little correlation with the evaluated quality signals. We estimate that tens of millions of high-quality pages remain among known but uncrawled URLs in each crawl examined, with most concentrated on a small share of hosts.
summaryZh: 本文探讨了如何优化网络爬虫在预训练数据采集中的资源分配策略。研究发现，通过对主机进行采样并优先抓取高质量样本，比传统的基于图中心度或均匀深度分配策略能更高效地获取高质量数据。该分析为构建更具成本效益的预训练数据集提供了数据驱动的策略建议。

aiReview.reasonZh: 该研究通过模拟分析优化了LLM预训练数据的采集策略，对提升数据质量和采集效率具有参考意义。
